Nor anyone who does what is detestable or false. Key words. “Detestable” (bdelygma, abomination, especially idolatry) and “false” (pseudos, lie). The sins of Babylon and the beast.

But only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life. Key words. The one qualification for entry: belonging to the Lamb. Not good works, not nationality, not religious heritage, but the Lamb’s choice and the Lamb’s blood. Those whose names were written before the foundation of the world (13:8; 17:8).

What it does not mean. The exclusion of the unclean does not mean that sinners can never enter. All who enter were once unclean, and were washed in the Lamb’s blood (7:14; 22:14). The city is closed to sin, not to sinners who have been cleansed.

In a sentence. The glory and honour of the nations will be brought into it; but nothing impure will ever enter it, nor anyone who does what is shameful or deceitful, only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

For worship. If your name is written in the Lamb’s book, the gates of pearl are open to you. Thank him, and live clean in the light of that day.

21.text: <sup>1</sup>Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more.<sup>2</sup>And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.<sup>3</sup>And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, “Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God.<sup>4</sup>He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away.”<sup>5</sup>And he who was seated on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.” Also he said, “Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.”<sup>6</sup>And he said to me, “It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the thirsty I will give from the spring of the water of life without payment.<sup>7</sup>The one who conquers will have this heritage, and I will be his God and he will be my son.<sup>8</sup>But as for the cowardly, the faithless, the detestable, as for murderers, the sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars, their portion will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur, which is the second death.”<sup>9</sup>Then came one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues and spoke to me, saying, “Come, I will show you the Bride, the wife of the Lamb.”<sup>10</sup>And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great, high mountain, and showed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God,<sup>11</sup>having the glory of God, its radiance like a most rare jewel, like a jasper, clear as crystal.<sup>12</sup>It had a great, high wall, with twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and on the gates the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel were inscribed—<sup>13</sup>on the east three gates, on the north three gates, on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.<sup>14</sup>And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.<sup>15</sup>And the one who spoke with me had a measuring rod of gold to measure the city and its gates and walls.<sup>16</sup>The city lies foursquare, its length the same as its width. And he measured the city with his rod, 12,000 stadia. Its length and width and height are equal.<sup>17</sup>He also measured its wall, 144 cubits by human measurement, which is also an angel’s measurement.<sup>18</sup>The wall was built of jasper, while the city was pure gold, like clear glass.<sup>19</sup>The foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with every kind of jewel. The first was jasper, the second sapphire, the third agate, the fourth emerald,<sup>20</sup>the fifth onyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.<sup>21</sup>And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, each of the gates made of a single pearl, and the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.<sup>22</sup>And I saw no temple in the city, for its temple is the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb.<sup>23</sup>And the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and its lamp is the Lamb.<sup>24</sup>By its light will the nations walk, and the kings of the earth will bring their glory into it,<sup>25</sup>and its gates will never be shut by day—and there will be no night there.<sup>26</sup>They will bring into it the glory and the honor of the nations.<sup>27</sup>But nothing unclean will ever enter it, nor anyone who does what is detestable or false, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

22.title: Come, Lord Jesus: The River, the Tree, and the Final Invitation
22.overview:
The final chapter of Revelation — and of the entire Bible — has the quality of a great symphony resolving into its final chord. Everything that has been promised, everything that has been anticipated, every thread of the biblical story, gathers here and arrives. The river of the water of life. The tree of life with twelve kinds of fruit. The servants of God seeing his face. His name on their foreheads. No more night. And then, three times: ‘I am coming soon.’ And the great response of the church across all the ages: ‘Come, Lord Jesus.’

The chapter is framed by the river and tree (vv. 1–5) and the final testimony and invitation (vv. 6–21). The garden returns — but infinitely elevated. Eden had a river flowing from it (Genesis 2:10); the new Jerusalem has a river flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb. Eden had the tree of life (Genesis 2:9); the new Jerusalem has the tree of life bearing twelve kinds of fruit, one each month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. What was lost in the garden is restored in the city, but the city is greater than the garden: the tree is no longer guarded by cherubim with flaming swords (Genesis 3:24) — it stands in the middle of the street, its fruit available to all.

The closing testimony of the book weaves together three voices: the angel confirming the truth of what has been shown, Jesus speaking in the first person (‘I, Jesus, have sent my angel...’; ‘I am coming soon’), and the Spirit and Bride together issuing the great invitation: ‘Come.’ The book ends not with explanation but with longing — the longing of the church for her Lord, the longing of the Lord for his people, the longing of the Spirit for the consummation of all things. This is the last word of the Bible, and it is the word the whole church has been praying for two thousand years: Come.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–5 — The River and the Tree of Life
verseByVerse.sectionOverview:
Verses 1–2: the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb down the middle of the street; and on either side of it the tree of life, bearing twelve crops a year, and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations (cf. Ezek. 47:1–12). The Bible has been away from a river and a tree since Genesis 3, where cherubim with a flaming sword were set to guard the way to the tree of life (Gen. 2:9–10; 3:24). The promise made to Ephesus in the first letter (2:7) is being kept.

Verse 3: No longer will there be anything accursed — the sentence of Genesis 3:17–19 lifted — but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. Verse 4: They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. Verse 5: no night, no need of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.
verseByVerse.theology:
The River and the Tree

The river of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life stands open with fruit every month and leaves for the healing of the nations. The curse is gone, and his servants will see his face.
verseByVerse.examples:
Then: The way to the tree, guarded since Eden, stands open in the middle of the street.

Now: Heaven is not first a place but a face — seen at last, and lived through.

verseByVerse.quote: Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb through the middle of the street of the city; also, on either side of the river, the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit each month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb through the middle of the street of the city; also, on either side of the river, the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit each month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.

Meaning first. Revelation 22 finishes the vision of the new creation and closes the book, and the whole Bible. The angel shows John the river of the water of life flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb, and the tree of life on both banks, bearing fruit every month, with leaves for the healing of the nations (vv. 1–2). There is no more curse; God’s servants will worship him, see his face, bear his name, live in his light and reign for ever (vv. 3–5). Then the epilogue: the angel assures John that these words are trustworthy and true, and Christ says, I am coming soon; blessed is the one who keeps the words of this book (vv. 6–7). John falls to worship the angel again and is told, worship God (vv. 8–9). He is told not to seal up the book, for the time is near; people will go on as they are (vv. 10–11). Christ declares that he is coming soon with his reward, that he is the Alpha and the Omega, and blesses those who wash their robes, who may enter the city, while outside are the wicked (vv. 12–15). Jesus himself speaks: he sent his angel for the churches, and he is the root and descendant of David, the bright morning star (v. 16). The Spirit and the bride say, Come, and everyone who is thirsty is invited to take the water of life freely (v. 17). A solemn warning forbids anyone to add to or take away from the book (vv. 18–19). And the book ends: Surely I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all (vv. 20–21). The Bible that began in a garden with a tree of life ends in a garden-city with the tree of life, God’s people seeing his face, and the prayer for Christ to come.

Setting and background. In Eden, a river flowed out to water the garden, and the tree of life stood in the midst of it (Genesis 2:9–10). After the fall, the way to the tree of life was barred by cherubim (Genesis 3:22–24). Ezekiel 47:1–12 describes a river flowing from the temple, growing deeper, bringing life wherever it goes, with trees on both banks whose fruit does not fail, bearing every month, and whose leaves are for healing. Zechariah 14:8 promises living waters flowing out from Jerusalem. Jesus promised that out of the heart of the one who believes in him will flow rivers of living water, meaning the Spirit (John 7:38–39).

Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, bright as crystal. Key words. “River of the water of life” (potamon hydatos zōēs). Eternal life, abundant and flowing. “Bright as crystal” (lampron hōs krystallon): pure, clear, shining. The promise of 7:17 and 21:6 fulfilled.

Flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb. Key words. One throne shared by God and the Lamb. Life flows from God’s rule. The source of all life is God himself, through the Lamb, by the Spirit (John 7:39).

Through the middle of the street of the city. Key words. The river runs down the main street. Life is at the centre of the city’s life.

Also, on either side of the river, the tree of life. Key words. “Tree of life” (xylon zōēs). What Adam and Eve lost is restored, as promised to Ephesus (2:7). “On either side”: perhaps a whole avenue of trees of life, or one tree spanning the river. The word for tree (xylon, wood) is also used of the cross (Acts 5:30; 1 Peter 2:24); by the tree on which Christ died, we have access to the tree of life.

With its twelve kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit each month. Key words. Constant abundance. Twelve: the number of God’s people. Fruit every month: no more seasons of want or scarcity. Ezekiel 47:12 says its fruit will not fail.

The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations. Key words. “Healing” (therapeian, health, healing; our word therapy comes from it). Not that there is sickness in the new creation, but that the leaves sustain the full health and wholeness of the nations. All the wounds of history, between nations and peoples, are healed. Ezekiel 47:12 says its leaves are for healing.

What it does not mean. The healing does not mean there will be illness or injury in the new creation that needs curing. There is no more pain (21:4). It means the nations enjoy perfect, lasting wholeness, the healing of all that sin had broken.

In a sentence. Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, sparkling like crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb down the middle of the city’s main street; on each side of the river stood the tree of life, producing twelve crops of fruit, a fresh crop every month, and its leaves are for the healing of the nations.

For worship. What Adam lost, Christ restores, and more. Thank him for the tree of life, opened to you by the tree on which he died.
verseByVerse.note: Eden’s river and tree of life return, now in a city.

verseByVerse.quote: No longer will there be anything accursed, but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.
verseByVerse.commentary:
No longer will there be anything accursed, but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.

Setting and background. After the fall, God cursed the ground because of Adam’s sin (Genesis 3:17). Zechariah 14:11 promises that there shall never again be a decree of utter destruction (curse) on Jerusalem. Moses asked to see God’s glory and was told, you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live (Exodus 33:20). The high priest’s blessing asked that the LORD make his face shine on his people (Numbers 6:24–26). Jesus said, blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God (Matthew 5:8). John wrote that when Christ appears we shall be like him, because we shall see him as he is (1 John 3:2).

No longer will there be anything accursed. Key words. “Accursed” (katathema, curse, anything under a curse). The curse of Genesis 3 is completely removed. Christ became a curse for us (Galatians 3:13), so that the curse could be lifted for ever. Everything that sin brought, death, pain, toil, decay, enmity, is gone.

But the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it. Key words. God reigns at the centre of the new creation. His rule is the source of its life and peace.

And his servants will worship him. Key words. “Servants” (douloi). “Worship” (latreusousin, serve as priests, worship). “Him” (singular): God and the Lamb together as one. Eternal life is worship and service, freely and joyfully given.

They will see his face. Key words. “See his face” (opsontai to prosōpon autou). The highest blessing in all of Scripture: the beatific vision, seeing God face to face. What Moses could not have, and what the wicked beg to be hidden from (6:16), the redeemed will enjoy for ever. To see his face is to know him fully, be fully known, and be fully accepted (1 Corinthians 13:12).

And his name will be on their foreheads. Key words. As in 3:12, 7:3 and 14:1. They belong to him completely, publicly and for ever. Like the high priest, who wore God’s name on his forehead (Exodus 28:36–38), all God’s people are priests in his presence.

And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light. Key words. As in 21:23–25. God himself is their light.

And they will reign forever and ever. Key words. “Reign” (basileusousin). Not for a thousand years only, but for ever and ever. The promise of Daniel 7:18, 27 that the saints of the Most High will possess the kingdom for ever. Adam was made to rule over creation under God (Genesis 1:26–28); redeemed humanity will finally fulfil that calling.

What it does not mean. Reigning for ever does not mean believers become rulers over one another, or over God. They reign with Christ, under God, over a renewed creation, as God always intended.

In a sentence. There will be no more curse; the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his servants will worship him; they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads; there will be no more night, and they will not need lamplight or sunlight, because the Lord God will shine on them, and they will reign for ever and ever.

For worship. The goal of everything is to see God’s face. Long for it, pray for it, and let that hope shape everything you do.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview:
Verses 6–7: the vision is over and the book begins closing itself by matching its own opening — the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place (cf. 1:1). Then the speaker changes without warning: And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book — the sixth beatitude, almost word for word the first one at 1:3.

Verses 8–9: John falls down to worship the angel a second time and is stopped a second time, in almost the words of 19:10 — I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.

Verses 10–11: Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near — the exact reverse of what Daniel was told (Dan. 12:4, 9) — followed by the hardest verse in the chapter: Let the evildoer still do evil… and the holy still be holy.

Verses 12–13: the second I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay each one for what he has done (cf. Isa. 40:10), and three pairs of titles: Alpha and Omega, first and last, beginning and end. Verses 14–15: the seventh and last beatitude — Blessed are those who wash their robes — and the list of those outside, ending with everyone who loves and practices falsehood. Verse 16: I, Jesus, have sent my angel… I am the root and the descendant of David, the bright morning star.
verseByVerse.theology:
The Testimony of Jesus

The book closes as it opened: blessed is the one who keeps its words. The angel refuses John’s worship again — Worship God. The book is left unsealed, for the time is near. Jesus, the Alpha and Omega, root and descendant of David, the bright morning star, is coming soon; blessed are those who wash their robes.
verseByVerse.examples:
Then: The whole vision was given for the churches, to be read aloud in small rooms.

Now: While the door is open, ask which way your life is already heading.

verseByVerse.quote: And he said to me, "These words are trustworthy and true. And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place." "And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And he said to me, “These words are trustworthy and true. And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place.” “And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”

Setting and background. The epilogue (22:6–21) echoes the prologue (1:1–8): the chain of revelation, the angel, the servants, what must soon take place, the blessing on those who keep the words, and Christ’s coming. The book ends where it began.

And he said to me, These words are trustworthy and true. Key words. As in 21:5. The whole book is guaranteed.

And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets. Key words. “Spirits of the prophets” (tōn pneumatōn tōn prophētōn). God, who inspired the prophets, has inspired this book. Revelation stands in the line of the Old Testament prophets, with their authority (2 Peter 1:21).

Has sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place. Key words. As in 1:1. The revelation is for all God’s servants, not a spiritual elite.

And behold, I am coming soon. Key words. “Coming soon” (erchomai tachy). Christ himself speaks. Three times in this chapter (vv. 7, 12, 20). The great hope of the church.

Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book. Key words. The sixth beatitude, echoing the first (1:3). “Keeps” (tērōn, obeys, holds fast). Revelation is to be obeyed, not merely studied.

What it does not mean. “Soon” does not mean Christ was mistaken about the timing. From God’s point of view, the end has been near since the resurrection, and his apparent delay is patience (2 Peter 3:8–9). Every generation is to live as though he may come in its lifetime.

In a sentence. The angel said to me, These words are trustworthy and true; the Lord, the God who inspires the prophets, sent his angel to show his servants what must soon happen; and Jesus says: Look, I am coming soon! How blessed is the one who obeys the words of the prophecy in this book!

On a Tuesday. Ask what Revelation calls you to do, not only what it predicts: worship God alone, refuse the world’s idols, endure, witness and long for Christ.

verseByVerse.quote: I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I heard and saw them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who showed them to me, but he said to me, "You must not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God."
verseByVerse.commentary:
I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I heard and saw them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who showed them to me, but he said to me, “You must not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”

Setting and background. John made the same mistake in 19:10. In ancient law, a matter was established by eyewitness testimony (Deuteronomy 19:15). John’s Gospel and first letter stress eyewitness testimony: we have heard, we have seen with our eyes, we have touched (1 John 1:1–3; John 19:35; 21:24).

I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. Key words. John signs his testimony as an eyewitness. He did not invent these visions; he received them.

And when I heard and saw them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who showed them to me. Key words. A second time. The glory of what he had seen overwhelmed him. Even an apostle could make this mistake, and he records it honestly to warn us.

But he said to me, You must not do that! Key words. The same urgent warning as in 19:10.

I am a fellow servant with you and your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Key words. Angels, prophets and all obedient believers are fellow servants of God. No created being deserves worship.

Worship God. Key words. The book’s last command about worship, and its central message. Throughout Revelation, the choice is whom to worship: God and the Lamb, or the dragon and the beast. Worship God alone.

What it does not mean. Respect for God’s messengers, human or angelic, is right (1 Thessalonians 5:12–13). Worship is not. Revering a teacher, preacher or spiritual experience so highly that it takes the place of God is idolatry.

In a sentence. I, John, am the one who heard and saw all this; and when I had heard and seen it, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had been showing me these things; but he said to me, Do not do that! I am a servant like you and your brothers the prophets, and like all who obey the words of this book; worship God!

For worship. Worship God. Not your experiences, not your leaders, not even the good gifts he gives. Him alone.

verseByVerse.quote: And he said to me, "Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near. Let the evildoer still do evil, and the filthy still be filthy, and the righteous still do right, and the holy still be holy."
verseByVerse.commentary:
And he said to me, “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near. Let the evildoer still do evil, and the filthy still be filthy, and the righteous still do right, and the holy still be holy.”

Setting and background. Daniel was told to shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end, because his visions concerned the distant future (Daniel 8:26; 12:4, 9). Daniel 12:10 says many shall purify themselves, but the wicked shall act wickedly, and none of the wicked shall understand. Ezekiel 3:27 says, he who will hear, let him hear; and he who will refuse to hear, let him refuse.

And he said to me, Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near. Key words. “Do not seal” (mē sphragisēs). In contrast to Daniel. Daniel’s vision was for the far future; John’s is for now. The last days have begun. The book must be open, read and obeyed by the churches. (Only the seven thunders were sealed, 10:4.)

Let the evildoer still do evil, and the filthy still be filthy. Key words. Not a command to keep sinning, but a solemn warning. Time is short, and character is being fixed. Those who persistently refuse God’s call harden themselves, and when Christ comes, there will be no more opportunity to change. The present choices settle eternal destinies.

And the righteous still do right, and the holy still be holy. Key words. An encouragement: keep on in righteousness and holiness. Do not give up because the end seems delayed or the world seems to win.

What it does not mean. This is not fatalism, as if people cannot change. The very next verses invite everyone to come and drink (v. 17). It means that time is short, and that a life’s direction, if persisted in, becomes permanent. Today is the day to turn.

In a sentence. Then he told me, Do not seal up the words of the prophecy in this book, because the time is near; let the one who does wrong go on doing wrong, and the vile go on being vile; let the one who does right go on doing right, and the holy go on being holy.

On a Tuesday. Your daily choices are shaping who you will be for ever. Keep doing right and keep being holy, by God’s grace, even when it seems to make no difference.
verseByVerse.note: Daniel was told to seal his book until the end; John is told not to, because the time is near.

verseByVerse.quote: "Behold, I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay each one for what he has done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“Behold, I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay each one for what he has done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.”

Setting and background. Isaiah 40:10 and 62:11 say, behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him. Isaiah 44:6 and 48:12 say, I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no god. Jesus said the Son of Man will come with his angels in the glory of his Father, and then he will repay each person according to what he has done (Matthew 16:27).

Behold, I am coming soon. Key words. The second time in this chapter.

Bringing my recompense with me. Key words. “Recompense” (misthos, wages, reward). Christ brings with him the reward of his people and the judgement of the wicked.

To repay each one for what he has done. Key words. “What he has done” (to ergon, his work). Singular: the whole pattern of a life. As in 20:12–13.

I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end. Key words. All three titles together. God said “Alpha and Omega” in 1:8 and 21:6; Christ said “first and last” in 1:17 and 2:8. Now Christ claims all of them. The clearest statement in Revelation that Jesus shares the identity of the one God. The one who began all things will end them.

What it does not mean. Repaying each one for what he has done does not mean believers earn eternal life. The free gift of the water of life is offered without price (v. 17). The reward Christ brings is a gift of grace that crowns the works his grace produced (Ephesians 2:8–10).

In a sentence. Look, I am coming soon! I bring my reward with me, to repay everyone according to what they have done; I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.

For worship. Worship Jesus as the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, God himself, who began your story and will bring it to its end.

verseByVerse.quote: Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and that they may enter the city by the gates. Outside are the dogs and sorcerers and the sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and that they may enter the city by the gates. Outside are the dogs and sorcerers and the sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.

Setting and background. In Jewish usage, dogs were scavengers, unclean animals, and the word was a term of contempt for the immoral and for Gentiles (Deuteronomy 23:18, where a male cult prostitute is called a dog; Matthew 7:6; Philippians 3:2). Sinners were cast out of Israel’s camp (Leviticus 13:46).

Blessed are those who wash their robes. Key words. The seventh and last beatitude in Revelation. “Wash” (plynontes, present tense: keep washing). As in 7:14: robes washed white in the blood of the Lamb. The one who trusts in Christ’s blood for cleansing, continually.

So that they may have the right to the tree of life. Key words. “Right” (exousia, authority, right of access). What was barred in Genesis 3:24 is now open to those cleansed by the Lamb.

And that they may enter the city by the gates. Key words. Through the pearly gates, always open (21:25).

Outside are the dogs and sorcerers and the sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood. Key words. “Outside” (exō). As in 21:8. Those who persist in sin without repentance are excluded. “Loves and practices falsehood”: the followers of the father of lies. This does not mean they are just beyond the walls in the new creation; it means they are shut out of God’s presence, in the lake of fire (21:8).

Textual note. Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read “Blessed are they that do his commandments” (poiountes tas entolas autou) instead of “Blessed are those who wash their robes” (plynontes tas stolas autōn). The two phrases look similar in Greek capital letters. The best and earliest manuscripts read “wash their robes”, and this fits 7:14 exactly. The difference is significant: access to the tree of life comes by cleansing in Christ’s blood, not by law-keeping.

What it does not mean. Those outside are not a permanent group of people looking in. It is a vivid way of saying they have no part in the city. Nor are the sins listed beyond forgiveness: anyone who washes their robes in the Lamb’s blood, whatever their past, may enter.

In a sentence. How blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they have the right to the tree of life and can go through the gates into the city! Outside are the dogs, those who practise magic, the sexually immoral, murderers, idolaters and everyone who loves and practises lies.

On a Tuesday. Keep washing your robes: bring every sin to Christ, daily, and trust his blood to cleanse you. That is the way into the city.
verseByVerse.note: The last of the seven “blessed” sayings in Revelation. Some manuscripts read “do his commandments” for “wash their robes” (ESV note) — the reading of the King James Version.

verseByVerse.quote: "I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the churches. I am the root and the descendant of David, the bright morning star."
verseByVerse.commentary:
“I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the churches. I am the root and the descendant of David, the bright morning star.”

Setting and background. Isaiah 11:1, 10 promises a shoot from the stump of Jesse, the root of Jesse, who will stand as a banner for the peoples. Numbers 24:17 says a star shall come out of Jacob, and a sceptre shall rise out of Israel. Jesus asked how the Messiah can be David’s son if David calls him Lord (Matthew 22:41–45). Peter speaks of the morning star rising in our hearts (2 Peter 1:19).

I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the churches. Key words. “I, Jesus” (egō Iēsous). The only place in Revelation where Jesus names himself this way. He personally guarantees the whole book. “To you” (plural): to all the churches. “For the churches”: Revelation is a letter to the church, for every congregation in every age.

I am the root and the descendant of David. Key words. “Root” (rhiza): the source of David, as God, David’s Lord. “Descendant” (genos, offspring): the son of David, as man, born in his line. Both divine and human. As in 5:5.

The bright morning star. Key words. “Morning star” (ho astēr ho lampros ho prōinos): Venus, the brightest star in the sky before dawn, heralding the new day. Christ is the sign that the long night of this age is nearly over and the day of the new creation is about to dawn. As promised to Thyatira (2:28), the conqueror receives Christ himself.

What it does not mean. The morning star title does not compare Christ with Lucifer, the day star of Isaiah 14:12, as some have confused it. Christ is the true light; the fallen king of Babylon was a false one.

In a sentence. I, Jesus, have sent my angel to give you this testimony for the churches; I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright star of the morning.

For worship. Worship Jesus as David’s Lord and David’s son, the morning star whose rising means the night is nearly over.

verseByVerse.sectionOverview:
Verse 17: The Spirit and the Bride say, “Come.” And let the one who hears say, “Come.” And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life without price (cf. Isa. 55:1; John 4:14; 7:37). Verses 18–19: the covenant scribe’s closing warning against adding to or taking from the words of the prophecy (cf. Deut. 4:2; 12:32; Prov. 30:5–6), with penalties that fit the offences exactly.

Verse 20: He who testifies to these things says, “Surely I am coming soon.” — the last recorded words of Jesus Christ in the Bible — and the church’s answer, Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! Verse 21: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.
verseByVerse.theology:
Come

The Spirit and the Bride say, “Come”; whoever hears is to say it too; whoever is thirsty may take the water of life without price. The book is not to be added to or taken from. Jesus says, “Surely I am coming soon,” and the church answers, “Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!”
verseByVerse.examples:
Then: The earliest church prayed Marana tha — Our Lord, come.

Now: The most terrifying book in Scripture ends with grace, offered to all.

verseByVerse.quote: The Spirit and the Bride say, "Come." And let the one who hears say, "Come." And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life without price.
verseByVerse.commentary:
The Spirit and the Bride say, “Come.” And let the one who hears say, “Come.” And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life without price.

Setting and background. Isaiah 55:1 invites: come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and he who has no money, come, buy and eat. Jesus stood up at the Feast of Booths and cried out, if anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink (John 7:37). He said, come to me, all who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest (Matthew 11:28).

The Spirit and the Bride say, Come. Key words. “Come” (erchou). The Holy Spirit and the church speak together. They pray to Christ, Come (as in v. 20), longing for his return. And they invite the world to come to Christ. The church, filled with the Spirit, both prays for Christ’s coming and calls sinners to come to him.

And let the one who hears say, Come. Key words. Everyone who hears this book read in church (1:3) is to join the prayer and the invitation.

And let the one who is thirsty come. Key words. “Thirsty” (dipsōn). The invitation is to anyone who knows their need. Thirst is the only qualification.

Let the one who desires take the water of life without price. Key words. “Desires” (thelōn, wants, wills). “Without price” (dōrean, as a free gift). The book of judgement ends with an open invitation. The last offer in the Bible is free grace.

Where Christians differ: if salvation depends on God’s choice, is this invitation sincere? Some argue that if God has chosen who will be saved, a universal invitation is meaningless; others argue that the invitation proves people have free will to come in their own power. Verdict: the gospel invitation is sincere and is to be offered freely to everyone without exception. Whoever wants to may come, and no one who comes will be turned away (John 6:37). At the same time, no one comes unless the Father draws them (John 6:44), and those who come are those whose names were written in the Lamb’s book (13:8). God’s sovereign grace does not make the invitation less real; it makes it effective. The Spirit who says Come is the Spirit who gives the thirst and the will to come.

What it does not mean. “Without price” does not mean without cost to God. It cost the Lamb his life. It is free to us because it was paid in full by him.

In a sentence. The Spirit and the bride say, Come! and everyone who hears should say, Come! Let anyone who is thirsty come, and anyone who wants it take the water of life as a free gift.

On a Tuesday. Join the Spirit and the bride: invite someone this week to come to Christ. The water of life is still free.

verseByVerse.quote: I warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book, and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are described in this book.
verseByVerse.commentary:
I warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book, and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are described in this book.

Setting and background. Moses warned Israel: you shall not add to the word that I command you, nor take from it (Deuteronomy 4:2; 12:32). Proverbs 30:6 says, do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be found a liar. In the ancient world, authors and copyists sometimes added curses to their writings to prevent tampering. Revelation was the last book of the New Testament to be written, and it stands at the end of the Bible.

I warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book. Key words. “Warn” (martyrō, testify, solemnly declare). Probably Jesus himself speaking (v. 20: he who testifies to these things). “Everyone who hears”: every congregation and every reader.

If anyone adds to them, God will add to him the plagues described in this book. Key words. A play on words: add to the book, and God will add its plagues to you. Adding to God’s word means claiming new revelation, new teaching with divine authority, or twisting the book with false prophecy.

And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will take away his share in the tree of life and in the holy city. Key words. Taking away means removing, denying or ignoring parts of God’s word: its warnings, its judgements, its demands or its promises. The penalty is the loss of eternal life itself. Such a person shows they never truly belonged to the Lamb.

Where Christians differ: does this verse close the whole canon of Scripture? Strictly, the warning applies to the book of Revelation. Some therefore argue it says nothing about the rest of the Bible, while others claim continuing revelation through prophets, popes, councils or new scriptures, such as the Book of Mormon. Verdict: the direct reference is to Revelation, but it applies the principle of Deuteronomy 4:2 to the final book of the New Testament, written by the last living apostle, and it fittingly closes the whole canon. With the death of the apostles, the foundation was laid (Ephesians 2:20), and the faith was once for all delivered to the saints (Jude 3). God has spoken his final word in his Son (Hebrews 1:1–2). Scripture is complete and sufficient (2 Timothy 3:16–17). No later revelation, vision, tradition or book may be added to it with equal authority, and no part of it may be removed. This app holds that the canon is closed and Scripture alone is our final authority.

What it does not mean. The warning does not condemn faithful copying, translation or teaching of the Bible. It condemns deliberately adding false teaching to it or cutting out what we do not like.

In a sentence. I solemnly warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy in this book: if anyone adds anything to them, God will add to that person the plagues described in this book; and if anyone takes away anything from the words of this book of prophecy, God will take away from that person his share in the tree of life and in the holy city, which are described in this book.

On a Tuesday. Take the whole Bible seriously: do not add to it with your own ideas, and do not skip the parts you find hard. Let all of it shape you.

verseByVerse.quote: He who testifies to these things says, "Surely I am coming soon." Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.
verseByVerse.commentary:
He who testifies to these things says, “Surely I am coming soon.” Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.

Setting and background. The earliest Christians prayed in Aramaic, Maranatha, which means Our Lord, come! (1 Corinthians 16:22; Didache 10:6). Paul ended his letters with a grace blessing, and Revelation ends as a letter, as it began (1:4).

He who testifies to these things says, Surely I am coming soon. Key words. “He who testifies” (ho martyrōn): Jesus, the faithful witness (1:5). “Surely” (nai, yes, truly). The third and final “I am coming soon” in this chapter, the last words of Jesus in the Bible. A promise.

Amen. Key words. So be it. John responds for the church.

Come, Lord Jesus! Key words. “Come” (erchou). The church’s answer to Christ’s promise, the Greek form of Maranatha. The final prayer of the Bible. The prayer of a bride for her bridegroom, of a persecuted church for its deliverer, of a groaning creation for its renewal (Romans 8:22–23). This is how Christians should feel about Christ’s return: not fear, but longing.

The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Key words. “Grace” (charis): God’s undeserved favour in Christ. The book of judgement ends with grace, as the whole Bible does. Everything in it, from the first word to the last, rests on the grace of the Lord Jesus.

Amen. The last word of the Bible.

Textual note. The manuscripts differ on the last line. Some read “with all”; others, “with all the saints” (followed by the ESV footnote); others, followed by the King James Version, “with you all”. The meaning is essentially the same: grace for all God’s people. Some manuscripts omit the final Amen.

What it does not mean. “With all” does not mean that grace will save everyone regardless of faith. The blessing is for those who hear and keep the words of this book (1:3), the church to which it is addressed.

In a sentence. The one who gives this testimony says, Yes, I am coming soon; Amen, come, Lord Jesus! May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with all of you. Amen.

For worship. Make this your prayer every day: Come, Lord Jesus. And rest in his grace until he does.
verseByVerse.note: “Come, Lord Jesus” matches the Aramaic prayer Maranatha that Paul quotes.

The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.<sup>3</sup>No longer will there be anything accursed, but the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will worship him.<sup>4</sup>They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.<sup>5</sup>And night will be no more. They will need no light of lamp or sun, for the Lord God will be their light, and they will reign forever and ever.<sup>6</sup>And he said to me, “These words are trustworthy and true. And the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, has sent his angel to show his servants what must soon take place.”<sup>7</sup>“And behold, I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”<sup>8</sup>I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. Worship God.”<sup>10</sup>And he said to me, “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.<sup>11</sup>Let the evildoer still do evil, and the filthy still be filthy, and the righteous still do right, and the holy still be holy.”<sup>12</sup>“Behold, I am coming soon, bringing my recompense with me, to repay each one for what he has done.<sup>13</sup>I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.”<sup>14</sup>Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life and that they may enter the city by the gates.<sup>15</sup>Outside are the dogs and sorcerers and the sexually immoral and murderers and idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.<sup>16</sup>“I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify to you about these things for the churches.
